title: Recycling at School
description: Children start a recycling project at their school.
instructions: Read about the recycling project. Then choose the right answer.

paragraphs.text: 🌍 Last month, our school started a recycling project. Our headteacher said, 'We throw away too much rubbish, and it is bad for our planet.' Everyone in Class 5 wanted to help.

First, we put four big boxes in the playground. Each box has a different colour and a picture. The blue box is for paper, the green box is for glass, the yellow box is for plastic bottles, and the red box is for batteries.

Linh and Sam are the 'Recycling Captains'. Every morning, they check the boxes and put the right things in them. If someone puts a banana skin in the paper box, they take it out and explain the mistake.
Our teacher, Ms Green, told us that paper is made from trees. If we recycle paper, we can save many trees. We were very surprised when we heard that!

We also had a competition to make something new from old things. Mai made a pencil box from a plastic bottle, and Ben made a robot from empty cans. The robot had two bottle-top eyes and it looked very funny. Ben won first prize.

Now our school has a rubbish-free day every Friday. Children bring their lunch in boxes instead of plastic bags, and they drink water from their own bottles. The canteen has stopped using plastic cups, too.

After two months, we have collected over three hundred kilos of paper and plastic. The headteacher says that the money from selling it will buy new books for the library. We are proud of our project, and we are going to ask other schools to join us.
